newsitem.title: USA: Cunanan not a killer, mother says in TV interview.
newsitem.headline: Cunanan not a killer, mother says in TV interview.

text.p: The mother of alleged serial killer Andrew Cunanan said in a television interview on Monday that her son was a "saint" who could not have killed Italian designer Gianni Versace.

"It wasn't my son," Mary Ann Cunanan said on "Hard Copy," adding she believed Cunanan had been framed. She also told the syndicated magazine news show she was convinced Cunanan did not commit suicide on a Miami houseboat days after Versace's death.
"He didn't take his own life... He was murdered... to shut him up... by the Mafia," she said.
Police believe Cunanan was responsible for four other murders besides that of Versace, who was shot and killed outside his Miami Beach mansion last month.
But Mary Ann Cunanan, who lives in a San Diego suburb, insisted that Cunanan was no murderer. "The truth is that he was kind and gentle, couldn't hurt a fly," she told Hard Copy.
Her son, she added, was a "saint" who was finally free and in heaven.
The mother, giving her first interview since Cunanan's death, said she knew her son was a homosexual but he never admitted it and she "kept my mouth shut."
She said she discovered her son's secret when she found photographs, a "black book" and a book of matches from a gay bar. "I figured two and two makes four, I'm not ignorant," she said.

Mary Ann Cunanan told reporters earlier this year that her son was a "high class male prostitute," but when asked on Hard Copy about his reputed homosexual relations with older male companions she said, "He wasn't doing sex for money. He was a companion to the elderly, not for sex."
